overview: Nedoceratops is one of the most controversial ceratopsid names in the wiki. It is based on a single skull from the Lance Formation of Wyoming and has been interpreted either as a distinct chasmosaurine genus or as an unusual individual of Triceratops.

That uncertainty is the point of the profile: Nedoceratops is less a well-sampled animal than a case study in how palaeontologists decide whether differences in horns, frills and skull openings represent species, growth stage, injury or individual variation.

fossilSites.name: Lance Formation
fossilSites.note: Latest Cretaceous unit cited for the single skull historically assigned to Nedoceratops.

articles.title: Why it matters
articles.body: The genus sits at the centre of debates over Triceratops variation and whether some named ceratopsids are distinct taxa or unusual specimens.

articles.title: Taxonomic caution
articles.body: Treat Nedoceratops as provisionally distinct in the catalogue, but read its profile as a taxonomic problem rather than a stable, well-sampled dinosaur.

record.mya: latest Maastrichtian, about 67-66 million years ago
record.description: Nedoceratops hatcheri is founded on a single chasmosaurine skull from the Lance Formation of Wyoming. Its lack of a nasal horn and small frill openings have produced an unresolved debate over whether it is distinct or an unusual Triceratops.
facts: No postcranial skeleton is securely associated with the type.
Farke found diagnostic differences supporting validity.
Scannella and Horner interpreted the skull as transitional morphology within Triceratops ontogeny; neither view should be hidden.
record.taxonomicStatus: disputed: valid genus in some studies, unusual Triceratops in others

review.ageReviewNote: The Lance Formation specimen is latest Maastrichtian, immediately before the end-Cretaceous extinction.

sources.citation: Farke (2011), anatomy and taxonomic status of Nedoceratops
Scannella & Horner (2011), Nedoceratops as transitional morphology

residualUncertainty: Its generic validity remains actively disputed.
The only skull may include individual, pathological or ontogenetic variation.
Specialist confirmation is still required before this profile is marked primary-literature reviewed.

evidence.summary: Authoritative-source baseline only; skeletal completeness has not yet received a specimen-level literature review.
